attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.finance_budget. Business justification: Margin targets must reconcile against finance budgets containing gross_margin_projection, cogs_projection, and otb_amount. Retail finance and merchandising teams align margin targets to approved finan

attributes.name: buyer_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchandise buyer responsible for the category or department covered by this margin target. Enables accountability tracking and buyer-level margin performance reporting.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); Workday HCM

attributes.name: category_id
attributes.description: Reference to the product subcategory within the category (e.g., Jackets within Men's Outerwear) for which this margin target is set. Enables granular margin guardrail enforcement at the subcategory level.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); NRF Merchandise Hierarchy Standards

attributes.name: department_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchandise department (e.g., Grocery, Apparel, Electronics) to which this margin target applies. Aligns with Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) department hierarchy.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); NRF Merchandise Hierarchy Standards

attributes.name: financial_period_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.financial_period. Business justification: Margin targets are set and tracked by fiscal period for budget planning and variance reporting. planning_period_label and planning_period_type are denormalized text representations of the fiscal perio

attributes.name: location_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to store.location. Business justification: Retail financial planning sets margin targets at the individual store location level for store-specific P&L accountability. Location-level margin targets are used in store performance reviews and annu

attributes.name: merch_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to merchandising.merch_plan. Business justification: Margin targets operationalize the planned_margin_percent defined in merch_plan. Finance and merchandising teams reconcile margin_target against merch_plan during seasonal planning cycles. A retail dom

attributes.name: price_list_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pricing.price_list. Business justification: Margin targets are scoped to specific pricing frameworks. A margin target for EDLP pricing differs from one for Hi-Lo or clearance. Linking margin_target to price_list allows margin governance to be a

attributes.name: price_zone_id
attributes.description: Reference to the price zone for which this margin target applies. Price zones group stores or regions with similar competitive pricing environments. Enables zone-level margin governance in Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM).
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Pricing Standards

attributes.name: primary_margin_category_id
attributes.description: Reference to the product category within the department (e.g., Men's Outerwear, Fresh Produce, Laptops) for which this margin target is defined. Supports category management and assortment planning.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); NRF Category Management Standards

attributes.name: profit_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.profit_center. Business justification: Margin targets are set at profit center level for financial planning and performance tracking. Core retail process: profit center margin planning, budget setting, and actual-to-target variance analysi

attributes.name: season_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to merchandising.season. Business justification: Margin targets are set by planning season because seasonal merchandise has different cost structures and markdown expectations (Spring/Fall apparel, holiday electronics). Season-specific margin target

attributes.name: tier_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to loyalty.tier. Business justification: Retail financial planning sets tier-specific margin targets — e.g., lower margin floor for Platinum members to drive retention. Margin planning reports by loyalty tier require this FK to link financia

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which this margin target was formally approved by the authorized merchandise planning or finance leader. Required for audit trail and governance documentation.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or employee identifier of the merchandise planning or finance leader who formally approved this margin target. Supports governance, accountability, and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: Internal Audit Standards; FASB ASC 606; NRF Governance Standards

attributes.name: asp_target
attributes.description: Planned Average Selling Price (ASP) for the category or subcategory during the planning period, in the denominated currency. ASP accounts for all promotional and markdown events and may differ from AUR when mix effects are significant.
attributes.references: NRF Retail KPI Standards; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR)

attributes.name: aur_target
attributes.description: Planned Average Unit Retail (AUR) price point for the category or subcategory during the planning period, in the denominated currency. AUR is a key retail KPI representing the average selling price per unit and is used to validate margin targets against pricing strategy.
attributes.references: NRF Retail KPI Standards; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM)

attributes.name: brand_classification
attributes.description: Classifies the brand type for which this margin target applies. 'private_label' refers to store-owned brands; 'national_brand' refers to manufacturer brands; 'exclusive_brand' refers to retailer-exclusive third-party brands; 'licensed_brand' refers to licensed intellectual property brands. Supports private label vs. national brand differential margin targeting.
attributes.references: NRF Private Label Standards; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

attributes.name: budget_utilization_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of the total markdown budget that has been consumed, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.6500 = 65.00%). Calculated as consumed markdown budget divided by total markdown budget. Used to monitor markdown pacing against plan.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Financial Planning Standards

attributes.name: channel
attributes.description: The retail channel to which this margin target applies. 'all' means the target spans all channels; 'store' means brick-and-mortar only; 'ecommerce' means digital commerce only; 'bopis' means Buy Online Pick Up In Store (BOPIS); 'wholesale' means B2B wholesale channel.
attributes.references: NRF Omnichannel Standards; Salesforce Commerce Cloud

attributes.name: cogs_rate_pct
attributes.business_glossary_term: Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) Rate Percentage
attributes.description: Planned Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) as a percentage of net sales for the planning period, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.5800 = 58.00%). Complements the gross margin target and is used for cost-plus margin validation in Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM).
attributes.references: FASB ASC 330 Inventory; SAP S/4HANA CO Module; NRF Financial Planning Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this margin target record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail, data lineage, and compliance reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); Internal Audit Standards

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which all monetary margin target values (markdown budget, etc.) are denominated (e.g., 'USD', 'GBP', 'EUR'). Supports multi-currency retail operations.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; GS1 Global Standards

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which this margin target expires and is no longer binding. Nullable for open-ended targets. Marks the close of the planning period for OTB and markdown budget reconciliation.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 606 Revenue Recognition; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM)

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The calendar date from which this margin target becomes active and binding for pricing governance and markdown budget control. Aligns with the start of the planning period.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 606 Revenue Recognition; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM)

attributes.name: gmroi_target
attributes.business_glossary_term: Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI) Target
attributes.description: Planned Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI) threshold for the planning period, expressed as a ratio (e.g., 2.5000 = $2.50 gross margin per $1.00 of average inventory investment). Used to evaluate inventory productivity and pricing efficiency.
attributes.references: NRF GMROI Standards; FASB ASC 330 Inventory; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

attributes.name: is_locked
attributes.description: Indicates whether this margin target record is locked and cannot be further revised. When True, the target is frozen for the planning period and no additional budget revisions are permitted. Used to enforce financial close controls.
attributes.references: Internal Audit Standards; FASB ASC 606; SAP S/4HANA FI Module

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp of the most recent modification to this margin target record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change detection, incremental ETL processing, and audit trail maintenance.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); Internal Audit Standards

attributes.name: markdown_budget_consumed
attributes.description: Actual markdown dollars consumed against the total markdown budget as of the last refresh. Tracks cumulative markdown spend to date within the planning period, enabling real-time budget utilization monitoring.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); SAP S/4HANA CO Module; FASB ASC 606

attributes.name: markdown_budget_remaining
attributes.description: Remaining markdown budget available for the planning period, calculated as total markdown budget minus consumed markdown budget. Provides planners with real-time visibility into available markdown capacity.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF OTB Planning Standards

attributes.name: markdown_budget_total
attributes.description: Total planned markdown budget in currency units allocated for the planning period, equivalent to the Open-to-Buy (OTB) markdown dollars. Represents the maximum allowable markdown spend to achieve sell-through targets without breaching margin floors.
attributes.references: NRF OTB Planning Standards; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FASB ASC 606

attributes.name: markdown_optimization_strategy
attributes.description: The pricing and markdown strategy governing how markdowns are applied within this margin target. 'edlp' = Everyday Low Price (EDLP); 'hi_lo' = High-Low promotional pricing; 'clearance' = end-of-season clearance markdown; 'dynamic' = algorithmic dynamic pricing; 'cost_plus' = cost-plus margin-based pricing.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Pricing Standards; FTC Pricing Transparency Standards

attributes.name: minimum_margin_floor_pct
attributes.description: The absolute minimum acceptable gross margin percentage below which pricing decisions must not fall, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.2500 = 25.00%). Acts as a hard pricing guardrail to prevent margin erosion during markdowns or promotional events.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 606; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF Pricing Standards

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for category managers or merchandise planners to capture contextual notes, assumptions, or exceptions related to this margin target, such as competitive market conditions, supplier cost changes, or seasonal demand anomalies.
attributes.references: NRF Merchandise Planning Standards; Internal Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: private_label_margin_premium_pct
attributes.description: The incremental gross margin percentage premium targeted for private label (store brand) products over national brand equivalents, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0800 = 8.00% premium). Supports private label vs. national brand differential margin strategy.
attributes.references: NRF Private Label Standards; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM)

attributes.name: revision_number
attributes.description: Sequential revision counter tracking how many times this margin target record has been revised or updated. Revision 0 represents the original plan; each subsequent revision increments by 1. Supports budget revision history and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 606; Internal Audit Standards; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM)

attributes.name: revision_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description of the business reason for the most recent revision to this margin target, such as 'Competitive price response', 'Seasonal demand shift', or 'Inventory clearance event'. Supports audit trail and governance documentation.
attributes.references: Internal Audit Standards; FASB ASC 606; FTC Pricing Transparency Standards

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this margin target originated. 'RPM' = Oracle Retail Price Management; 'ORMS' = Oracle Retail Merchandising System; 'SAP' = SAP S/4HANA; 'MANUAL' = manually entered by a planner.
attributes.references: Informatica MDM; Internal Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: source_system_ref_code
attributes.description: The native identifier of this margin target record in the originating operational system (e.g., Oracle RPM plan ID, SAP cost center plan number). Enables cross-system traceability and reconciliation.
attributes.references: Informatica MDM; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); SAP S/4HANA

attributes.name: target_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric business identifier for the margin target record, used in Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) and SAP S/4HANA for cross-system reference and audit trail linkage.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); GS1 Data Standards

attributes.name: target_gross_margin_pct
attributes.description: Planned gross margin percentage for the defined scope and planning period, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.4200 = 42.00%). Calculated as (Net Sales - COGS) / Net Sales. Serves as the primary pricing guardrail for category managers and merchandise planners.
attributes.references: FASB ASC 606; NRF Financial Planning Standards; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM)

attributes.name: target_name
attributes.description: Human-readable descriptive name for the margin target plan, such as 'Q2 FY2025 Electronics Gross Margin Target' or 'Holiday Season Apparel Markdown Budget'. Used by category managers and merchandise planners for identification.

attributes.name: target_sell_through_rate_pct
attributes.description: Planned sell-through rate (percentage of inventory sold) for the planning period, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.8500 = 85.00%). Used in conjunction with markdown budget to optimize markdown timing and depth to achieve margin targets.
attributes.references: NRF Inventory Planning Standards; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

attributes.name: target_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the margin target record. 'draft' indicates under construction; 'active' means currently governing pricing decisions; 'approved' means signed off by finance/merchandising leadership; 'superseded' means replaced by a revised target; 'closed' means the planning period has ended; 'cancelled' means the target was voided.
attributes.references: NRF Retail Merchandise Planning Standards; Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM)

attributes.name: target_weeks_of_supply
attributes.description: Planned Weeks of Supply (WOS) — the number of weeks of inventory coverage targeted at the end of the planning period. Used alongside margin targets to balance inventory investment and markdown risk.
attributes.references: NRF Inventory Planning Standards; Blue Yonder Demand Planning; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS)

products.name: price_override
products.description: Records point-of-sale and e-commerce price overrides applied at the transaction level. Captures override type (manager discount, price match, damaged goods, loyalty benefit, error correction), original price, override price, override amount or percentage, reason code, authorizing employee, store or channel, and transaction reference. Supports shrinkage monitoring, discount abuse detection, and override variance analysis.

attributes.name: price_override_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for each price override record applied at the point-of-sale or e-commerce transaction level. Primary key for this entity.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR)

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Price overrides are tracked by cost center for shrink analysis and policy compliance. Business process: override accountability by department, margin impact tracking, and internal controls for pricing

attributes.name: location_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the physical store or fulfillment location where the price override was applied. Used for store-level override variance analysis and shrinkage monitoring.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); SAP S/4HANA Retail

attributes.name: loyalty_membership_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to loyalty.membership. Business justification: Price overrides are frequently granted based on membership status/tier (VIP price matching, tier-based discretionary discounts). Existing profile_id lacks tier/status context. Supports member-specific

attributes.name: pos_terminal_id
attributes.description: The identifier of the Point of Sale (POS) terminal or register where the override was applied. Used for terminal-level override frequency analysis and shrinkage monitoring. Populated for in-store channel overrides; null for e-commerce.
attributes.references: SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR); PCI DSS; NRF

attributes.name: pos_transaction_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Point of Sale (POS) or e-commerce transaction in which this price override was applied. Links the override to its originating sales event in SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR) or Salesforce Commerce Cloud.
attributes.references: SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR); Salesforce Commerce Cloud

attributes.name: price_list_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pricing.price_list. Business justification: A price override is applied in the context of a specific price list (e.g., EDLP base, Hi-Lo promotional). Linking price_override to price_list allows auditors and analysts to understand which pricing

attributes.name: price_zone_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the pricing zone associated with the store or channel where the override occurred. Used to contextualize the override against the applicable zone-level pricing strategy in Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM).

attributes.name: profile_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the customer who received the price override benefit, if applicable. Populated for loyalty benefit overrides, price match requests, and personalized discount events. May be null for anonymous transactions.
attributes.references: Salesforce Commerce Cloud; Informatica MDM; GDPR Article 4; CCPA

attributes.name: program_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the customer loyalty program under which the price override benefit was granted, applicable when override_type is 'loyalty_benefit'. Links to the loyalty program master for Customer Lifetime Value (CLTV) and Recency Frequency Monetary (RFM) analysis.
attributes.references: Salesforce Commerce Cloud; Informatica MDM; GDPR Article 4; CCPA

attributes.name: promo_offer_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the promotional event or campaign that authorized or triggered the price override, if applicable. Links to the promotion master for markdown optimization and promotional Return on Investment (ROI) analysis.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); Salesforce Commerce Cloud; NRF

attributes.name: rule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pricing.rule. Business justification: The rule entity defines whether overrides are permitted (override_permitted, override_approval_required fields). Linking price_override to the governing rule enables enforcement auditing — which rule

attributes.name: sku_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the product (Stock Keeping Unit / SKU) whose price was overridden. Links to the product master in Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) or Informatica MDM.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); Informatica MDM; GS1

attributes.name: sku_price_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to pricing.sku_price. Business justification: A price override at POS or e-commerce overrides a specific authoritative sku_price record. Linking price_override to sku_price enables direct traceability from the override event back to the resolved

attributes.name: approval_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this override type or amount threshold required explicit manager authorization before being applied at the Point of Sale (POS). Drives workflow routing in Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) and supports discount abuse detection controls.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); Internal Audit Policy; NRF

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the authorizing employee approved the price override. Null if approval was not required or if the override is still pending. Used for approval latency analysis and audit trail compliance.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); ISO 8601; Internal Audit Policy

attributes.name: channel
attributes.description: The retail channel through which the price override was applied. Supports omnichannel override analysis across physical stores, e-commerce (Salesforce Commerce Cloud), mobile, Buy Online Pick Up In Store (BOPIS), and other touchpoints.
attributes.references: Salesforce Commerce Cloud; SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR); NRF

attributes.name: competitor_name
attributes.description: Name of the competing retailer whose price was matched, applicable when override_type is 'price_match'. Supports competitive pricing intelligence and price match policy compliance reporting.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FTC Pricing Transparency Standards; NRF

attributes.name: competitor_price
attributes.description: The price offered by the competing retailer that was matched, applicable when override_type is 'price_match'. Used to validate price match eligibility and support competitive pricing analytics in Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM).
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FTC Pricing Transparency Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this price override record was first created and persisted in the Silver Layer of the Databricks Lakehouse. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and reconciliation purposes.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; ISO 27001; Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary amounts on this override record (e.g., USD, CAD, GBP). Supports multi-currency retail operations and financial reporting.

attributes.name: exceeds_threshold
attributes.description: Indicates whether the override amount or percentage exceeded the authorizing employee's configured override limit threshold. True triggers escalation workflow and flags the record for discount abuse review.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); Internal Audit Policy; NRF

attributes.name: original_price
attributes.description: The regular or shelf price of the item before the override was applied, as defined in Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM). Represents the Average Unit Retail (AUR) or Everyday Low Price (EDLP) baseline used to calculate override variance and markdown impact.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FASB ASC 606; FTC Pricing Transparency

attributes.name: override_amount
attributes.description: The absolute monetary value of the price reduction applied by the override, calculated as original_price minus override_price. Used for markdown optimization, shrinkage monitoring, and Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI) impact analysis.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FASB ASC 606; NRF

attributes.name: override_limit_threshold
attributes.description: The maximum monetary amount or percentage discount that the authorizing employee's role is permitted to apply without escalation, as configured in Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM). Used to flag overrides that exceeded authorization limits for discount abuse detection.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); Internal Audit Policy; NRF

attributes.name: override_percentage
attributes.description: The price override expressed as a percentage discount relative to the original price (override_amount / original_price * 100). Used for threshold-based discount abuse detection rules and override variance reporting.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF; Internal Audit Policy

attributes.name: override_price
attributes.description: The final selling price applied to the item after the override, as recorded at the Point of Sale (POS) or e-commerce checkout. This is the price the customer was charged and the value recognized for revenue reporting under FASB ASC 606.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FASB ASC 606; FTC Pricing Transparency

attributes.name: override_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally visible alphanumeric reference number assigned to this price override event, used for audit trail tracking, customer receipts, and reconciliation with Point of Sale (POS) systems and Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM).
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR); NRF

attributes.name: override_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the price override record. 'applied' indicates the override was executed at POS; 'pending_approval' indicates it awaits manager authorization; 'rejected' indicates it was denied; 'voided' indicates it was cancelled before completion; 'reversed' indicates a post-transaction correction was made.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF; Internal Audit Policy

attributes.name: override_timestamp
attributes.description: The exact date and time when the price override was applied at the Point of Sale (POS) terminal or e-commerce checkout. This is the principal business event timestamp for this transaction record, recorded in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).
attributes.references: SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR); ISO 8601; NRF

attributes.name: override_type
attributes.description: Classification of the business reason driving the price override. 'manager_discount' is a discretionary reduction authorized by a supervisor; 'price_match' is a competitive price adjustment; 'damaged_goods' is a markdown for defective or impaired merchandise; 'loyalty_benefit' is a discount applied via a customer loyalty program; 'error_correction' is a fix for a pricing system error.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF; FTC Pricing Transparency Standards

attributes.name: quantity
attributes.description: The number of units of the item to which the price override was applied within the transaction. Used to calculate total override impact and Units Per Transaction (UPT) analysis.
attributes.references: SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR); Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); NRF

attributes.name: reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized alphanumeric code from the Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) reason code table that identifies the specific business justification for the price override. Enables granular override variance analysis and discount abuse detection reporting.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); NRF; FTC

attributes.name: reason_description
attributes.description: Free-text narrative description entered by the authorizing employee to explain the business justification for the price override. Supplements the structured reason code with contextual detail for audit and investigation purposes.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); Internal Audit Policy

attributes.name: shrinkage_related
attributes.description: Indicates whether this price override is associated with a shrinkage event (e.g., damaged goods markdown, theft-related adjustment). Used for inventory shrinkage monitoring and loss prevention analytics.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); NRF; Internal Loss Prevention Policy

attributes.name: sku
attributes.description: The retailer-assigned Stock Keeping Unit code identifying the specific product variant (size, color, style) subject to the price override. Aligns with the GS1 product identification standard and Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) item master.
attributes.references: GS1; Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS); NRF

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record that originated this price override record. Supports data lineage tracking across SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR), Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM), Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC), and other integrated systems.
attributes.references: Informatica MDM; ISO 27001; Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: source_system_override_code
attributes.description: The native identifier assigned to this price override record in the originating operational system (e.g., SAP CAR document number, RPM override ID). Enables cross-system reconciliation and data lineage tracing.
attributes.references: SAP Customer Activity Repository (CAR); Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); Informatica MDM

attributes.name: total_override_impact
attributes.description: The total monetary impact of the price override across all units in the transaction line, calculated as override_amount multiplied by quantity. Represents the gross markdown exposure for financial reporting and Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI) analysis.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FASB ASC 606; NRF

attributes.name: upc
attributes.description: The 12-digit Universal Product Code barcode identifier for the item subject to the price override, as scanned at the Point of Sale (POS) terminal. Conforms to GS1 UPC-A standard.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this price override record, such as a status change, approval, reversal, or correction. Supports audit trail and change data capture (CDC) processing.
attributes.references: ISO 8601; ISO 27001; Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: void_reason
attributes.description: Free-text or coded explanation for why the price override was voided or reversed. Supports audit trail completeness and post-transaction correction analysis.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); Internal Audit Policy

attributes.name: void_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the price override was voided or reversed, if applicable. Null for active or applied overrides. Used for override lifecycle tracking and financial reconciliation.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM); FASB ASC 606; ISO 8601

products.name: cost_zone
products.description: Master reference table for cost_zone. Referenced by cost_zone_id.

attributes.name: cost_zone_id
attributes.description: Primary key for cost_zone

attributes.name: category_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to merchandising.category. Business justification: Cost zones in retail are frequently defined at the category level (e.g., produce cost zone, electronics cost zone) with category-specific freight and duty factors. Linking cost_zone to category enable

attributes.name: parent_cost_zone_id
attributes.description: Reference to a parent cost zone in a hierarchical cost zone structure, enabling nested or regional rollup of cost zones.

attributes.name: annual_revenue_amount
attributes.description: Estimated or actual annual revenue generated within this cost zone in the zone's currency.

attributes.name: annual_volume_units
attributes.description: Estimated or actual annual sales volume in units for this cost zone, used for cost allocation and pricing optimization.

attributes.name: approval_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether pricing changes in this cost zone require management approval before implementation.

attributes.name: approval_threshold_amount
attributes.description: Monetary threshold above which pricing changes in this zone require additional approval levels.

attributes.name: competitive_intensity
attributes.description: Level of competitive pressure in this cost zone affecting pricing flexibility and margin targets.

attributes.name: cost_adjustment_factor
attributes.description: Multiplier applied to base costs to account for zone-specific cost variations, typically ranging from 0.8 to 1.5.

attributes.name: cost_review_frequency
attributes.description: Scheduled frequency for reviewing and updating cost factors and margins for this cost zone.

attributes.name: cost_zone_code
attributes.description: Business identifier code for the cost zone used in pricing systems and external integrations. Typically alphanumeric and unique across the enterprise.

attributes.name: cost_zone_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the cost zone including its purpose, geographic coverage, and business rationale.

attributes.name: cost_zone_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the cost zone for display and reporting purposes.

attributes.name: cost_zone_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the cost zone indicating whether it is actively used in pricing calculations.

attributes.name: cost_zone_type
attributes.description: Classification of the cost zone based on the segmentation strategy used (geographic regions, sales channels, store formats, vendor agreements, product categories, or custom business rules).

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code indicating the primary country for this cost zone.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the cost zone record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code used for cost calculations within this zone.

attributes.name: default_cost_method
attributes.description: Primary costing methodology applied to products within this cost zone for inventory valuation and pricing calculations.

attributes.name: duty_factor_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage applied to base product cost to account for import duties and tariffs applicable to this cost zone.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date when the cost zone ceases to be active. Null indicates an open-ended cost zone with no planned expiration.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date when the cost zone becomes active and applicable for pricing calculations.

attributes.name: freight_factor_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage applied to base product cost to account for freight and transportation expenses specific to this cost zone.

attributes.name: geographic_scope
attributes.description: Geographic coverage level of the cost zone indicating the breadth of locations included.

attributes.name: hierarchy_level
attributes.description: Numeric level in the cost zone hierarchy where 1 represents the top level and higher numbers represent deeper nesting.

attributes.name: last_cost_review_date
attributes.description: Date when cost factors and pricing parameters for this zone were last reviewed and validated.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the cost zone record was last updated.

attributes.name: minimum_margin_percentage
attributes.description: Minimum acceptable gross margin percentage for products sold within this cost zone, used as a pricing floor constraint.

attributes.name: next_cost_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next cost review and potential adjustment of zone parameters.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-form text field for additional business context, special instructions, or historical information about the cost zone.

attributes.name: overhead_factor_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage applied to base product cost to account for warehousing, handling, and operational overhead costs in this zone.

attributes.name: pricing_strategy
attributes.description: Primary pricing strategy employed in this cost zone. EDLP (Everyday Low Price) maintains consistent low prices; Hi-Lo uses promotional pricing cycles.

attributes.name: store_count
attributes.description: Number of retail locations assigned to this cost zone for operational reporting and volume analysis.

attributes.name: target_margin_percentage
attributes.description: Target gross margin percentage that pricing strategies aim to achieve for products in this cost zone.

domains.name: promotion
domains.description: Manages promotional campaigns, deals, coupons, rebates, BOGO offers, seasonal sales events, circular ads, and digital promotions across channels. Tracks promotion effectiveness, redemption rates, incremental lift, promotional ROI, and vendor-funded promotion agreements. Distinct from pricing — promotions are time-bound, event-driven incentives. Supports omnichannel promotion execution across POS, e-commerce, and mobile apps.

products.name: promo_campaign
products.description: Master record for a promotional campaign representing a time-bound marketing initiative encompassing both the strategic campaign wrapper and discrete promotional sales events (Flash Sales, Doorbuster Events, Holiday Sales). Captures campaign name, type, start/end dates, event classification, budget, and performance targets.

attributes.name: promo_campaign_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the promotional campaign. Primary key.

attributes.name: assortment_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to merchandising.assortment_plan. Business justification: Retail buyers tie promotional campaigns to specific assortment plans during seasonal planning (e.g., new-item launch campaigns). The 'campaign-to-assortment alignment' report is a standard retail plan

attributes.name: brand_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.product_brand. Business justification: Brand-level promotional campaigns (e.g., 'Summer Pepsi Campaign', 'Nike Back-to-School') are a core retail/CPG process. Brand campaign planning, vendor co-op reporting, and brand promotional spend ana

attributes.name: buyer_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to merchandising.buyer. Business justification: In retail, buyers own promotional campaigns for their categories and negotiate vendor-funded promotions. Campaign performance reporting by buyer (ROI, redemption rate, margin impact) is a standard ret

attributes.name: category_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to merchandising.category. Business justification: Promotional campaigns are planned and executed at category level. Category managers need visibility to all campaigns targeting their categories for assortment planning, inventory positioning, and perf

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: FK to finance.cost_center

attributes.name: financial_period_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.financial_period. Business justification: Promo campaigns span fiscal periods; finance teams align campaign spend to financial periods for period-close and promotional ROI reporting. Retail finance requires campaign-level fiscal period attrib

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Campaign expenses must post to specific GL accounts for financial reporting. Every campaign has a default expense account (promotional allowances, markdown expense) required for proper accounting clas

attributes.name: item_hierarchy_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.item_hierarchy. Business justification: Campaigns target product categories/departments (e.g., 'Back to School - Electronics'). Budget allocation, buyer approval workflows, and performance rollup all operate at hierarchy level. Enables cate

attributes.name: ledger_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.ledger. Business justification: Promo campaign budgets and GL postings are made against a specific ledger in retail finance. Ledger attribution on promo_campaign ensures correct multi-GAAP reporting of promotional spend across leadi

attributes.name: member_segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to loyalty.member_segment. Business justification: promo_campaign.customer_segment_target is a plain-text denormalization of loyalty.member_segment. Campaign targeting, personalization reporting, and segment-level ROI analysis require a proper FK. Ret

attributes.name: parent_promo_campaign_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on promo_campaign (parent_promo_campaign_id)

attributes.name: profit_center_id

products.name: promo_redemption

attributes.name: budget_status

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp

attributes.name: notes

attributes.name: pos_channel_allocation

attributes.name: variance_threshold_percent

attributes.name: vendor_funded_amount
attributes.description: Portion of the total budget that is funded by vendor co-op agreements, trade promotion allowances, or supplier marketing development funds. Represents external funding contribution to the promotional budget.

products.name: promo_calendar
products.description: Master record for the retail promotional calendar defining planned promotional periods, key retail events, blackout dates, and competitive response windows for a fiscal year. Captures period name, period type (weekly ad cycle, seasonal event, holiday, clearance window, competitive response), start/end dates, fiscal week/month/quarter alignment, priority tier, planning lock date, planning status (draft, locked, active, archived), and banner/market applicability for multi-banner retailers. Used by merchandising, marketing, and supply chain teams to coordinate promotional activity, inventory positioning, and circular production timelines. Serves as the shared planning backbone that prevents promotional conflicts and ensures adequate lead time for vendor negotiations and inventory builds. Supports multi-banner coordination by allowing banner-specific or enterprise-wide calendar periods.

attributes.name: blackout_reason

domains.name: supplier
domains.description: Authoritative source for supplier and vendor master data including contact information, contracts, compliance certifications, performance scorecards, chargebacks (vendor compliance penalties), RTV (Return to Vendor) processes, EDI integration, MOQ and lead time agreements, and VMI configurations. Manages supplier onboarding, qualification, risk assessment, and ongoing relationship management for national brands, private label manufacturers, and DSD vendors.

products.name: vendor
products.description: Master record for all suppliers and vendors including national brand manufacturers, private label producers, DSD vendors, and 3PL partners. Serves as the authoritative golden record for vendor identity, classification, tax identifiers (W-9/W-8), remittance details, business type, ownership structure, diversity certifications, DUNS number, and onboarding status. Contains embedded contact persons (account managers, EDI coordinators, compliance contacts, executive sponsors) with role types, communication preferences, and escalation paths. Contains embedded multi-address records (headquarters, remittance, ship-from, RTV addresses) with geo-coordinates, address validation status, and address type classification. Sourced from Informatica MDM and SAP S/4HANA MM vendor master.

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the vendor. Primary key for the vendor master record.

domains.description: Manages strategic merchandise planning, assortment management, category management, OTB (Open to Buy) budgets, buying decisions, vendor negotiations, and seasonal planning. products.name: merch_plan
products.description: Master merchandise financial plan capturing OTB (Open to Buy) budgets, planned sales, planned inventory, planned margin, GMROI targets, and seasonal buying commitments by department, category, and season. The authoritative financial blueprint for buying decisions, assortment investments, and seasonal commitment tracking. Integrates with Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) merchandise planning module.

attributes.description: Timestamp when the buyer record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.description: Identifier of the source system from which the buyer record originated (e.g., ORMS for Oracle Retail Merchandising System, Workday for HR data). Used for data lineage and reconciliation.

attributes.name: division_code
attributes.description: Code representing the merchandising division to which the buyer belongs (e.g., Hardlines, Softlines, Grocery). Divisions are the highest level of merchandise organization.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Division Hierarchy

attributes.name: email_address
attributes.description: Primary corporate email address for the buyer. Used for vendor communications, purchase order approvals, and system notifications.

attributes.name: gmroi_target
attributes.business_glossary_term: Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI) Target
attributes.description: Target GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Investment) ratio assigned to the buyer for their assigned categories. Measures how much gross margin is generated for every dollar of inventory investment. Expressed as a ratio (e.g., 2.50 means $2.50 of gross margin per $1.00 of inventory).

attributes.name: hire_date
attributes.description: Date the buyer was hired into the organization. Used for tenure analysis and performance benchmarking.

attributes.name: international_sourcing_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the buyer is authorized to source products from international vendors and manage cross-border procurement. True if international sourcing is within scope.

attributes.name: inventory_turn_target
attributes.description: Target inventory turnover ratio assigned to the buyer for their assigned categories. Measures how many times inventory is sold and replaced over a period (typically annually). Higher turns indicate more efficient inventory management.

attributes.name: language_proficiency
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of languages the buyer is proficient in, relevant for international vendor negotiations and global sourcing activities.

attributes.name: last_modified_by_user
attributes.description: User ID or system identifier of the person or process that last modified the buyer record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the buyer record was last updated. Used for change tracking and audit compliance.

attributes.name: last_performance_review_date
attributes.description: Date of the buyer's most recent formal performance review. Used to track review cycles and identify buyers due for evaluation.

attributes.name: markdown_percentage_limit
attributes.description: Maximum allowable markdown percentage the buyer can authorize without additional approval. Expressed as a percentage of original retail price (e.g., 30.00 means up to 30% markdown is allowed).
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) - Markdown Policy

attributes.name: office_location_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the physical office or buying center where the buyer is based. Used for travel expense allocation and regional vendor assignments.

attributes.name: otb_budget_limit
attributes.description: Total OTB (Open to Buy) budget allocated to this buyer for the current fiscal period. Represents the maximum inventory investment the buyer can commit to across all assigned categories.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - OTB Planning

attributes.name: phone_number
attributes.description: Primary business phone number for the buyer. Used for vendor negotiations and internal escalations.

attributes.name: preferred_vendor_count
attributes.description: Number of preferred or strategic vendors the buyer actively manages relationships with. Used to assess vendor portfolio concentration and diversification strategy.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Vendor Management

attributes.name: private_label_focus_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the buyer has primary responsibility for private label (store brand) product development and sourcing. True if the buyer manages private label assortments.

attributes.name: sell_through_rate_target
attributes.description: Target sell-through rate percentage assigned to the buyer for their assigned categories. Represents the percentage of inventory that should be sold within a defined period (typically a season). Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 85.00 means 85% of inventory should sell through).

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: Date the buyer left the organization or was terminated. Null for active employees. Triggers reassignment of assigned categories and vendors.

attributes.name: vendor_negotiation_rating
attributes.description: Performance rating reflecting the buyer's effectiveness in negotiating favorable commercial terms with vendors. Based on achieved cost reductions, payment terms, and markdown allowances.

attributes.name: years_of_buying_experience
attributes.description: Total number of years the individual has worked in merchandise buying roles, including experience prior to joining the current organization. Used for capability assessment and succession planning.

products.name: season
products.description: Reference master for retail planning seasons and fiscal periods used to scope merchandise plans, OTB budgets, assortment plans, and buying commitments. Captures season code (e.g., SS24, FW24), season name, fiscal year, start and end dates, key milestone dates (line review, buy deadline, first receipt, markdown entry, clearance exit), and season status (planning, open-to-buy, in-season, post-season). Provides the temporal backbone for all merchandising planning and performance measurement.

attributes.name: season_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the retail planning season. Primary key.

attributes.name: financial_period_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.financial_period. Business justification: Retail seasons are directly aligned to fiscal periods for OTB budgeting, markdown timing, and period-close reconciliation. Season has fiscal_year as a plain attribute but no FK to financial_period. Re

attributes.name: assortment_breadth_target
attributes.description: The target number of distinct product categories to be carried during this season. Represents the range of categories. Drives overall merchandising strategy and store space allocation.

attributes.name: assortment_depth_target
attributes.description: The target number of SKUs (Stock Keeping Units) within each product category for this season. Represents the variety within categories. Drives category management and buying decisions.

attributes.name: buy_deadline_date
attributes.description: The final date by which all purchase orders for the season must be committed to vendors. Ensures timely receipt of merchandise for season launch.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Season Milestones

attributes.name: clearance_exit_date
attributes.description: The target date by which all seasonal merchandise should be sold through or removed from active selling floor. Marks the end of clearance activities.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) - Markdown Calendar

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the season record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the OTB budget and financial planning (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Ensures consistent financial reporting across regions.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: The date when the season officially ends. Marks the transition to post-season analysis and clearance activities.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Season Master

attributes.name: first_receipt_date
attributes.description: The target date for the first merchandise receipts to arrive at distribution centers or stores for the season. Marks the beginning of inventory flow.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Season Milestones

attributes.name: fiscal_year
attributes.description: The fiscal year to which this season belongs (e.g., 2024). Aligns season planning with financial reporting periods.

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the season is currently active for planning or operational use. True if the season is in planning, open-to-buy, or in-season status. False if post-season or closed.

attributes.name: line_review_date
attributes.description: Key milestone date when the merchandising team reviews and approves the product line assortment for the season. Critical gate for buying decisions.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Season Milestones

attributes.name: markdown_entry_date
attributes.description: The date when initial markdown pricing strategies are activated to accelerate sell-through of seasonal merchandise. Signals transition to promotional phase.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM) - Markdown Calendar

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for capturing additional context, strategic notes, or special considerations for the season (e.g., market trends, competitive landscape, promotional themes). Used by merchandising planners.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Season Master

attributes.name: otb_budget_amount
attributes.description: The total Open to Buy budget allocated for this season in the base currency. Represents the planned purchase commitment for merchandise. Critical for financial planning and vendor negotiations.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - OTB Planning

attributes.name: planning_start_date
attributes.description: The date when pre-season planning activities begin, including assortment planning, OTB (Open to Buy) budget allocation, and category strategy development.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Season Planning

attributes.name: season_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code representing the season (e.g., SS24 for Spring/Summer 2024, FW24 for Fall/Winter 2024). Used as the business identifier across merchandising systems.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Season Master

attributes.name: season_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the season (e.g., Spring/Summer 2024, Holiday 2024, Back-to-School 2024). Human-readable label for business users.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Season Master

attributes.name: season_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the season. Planning: pre-season planning phase. Open-to-Buy: OTB budgets active, buying in progress. In-Season: merchandise on floor, active selling. Post-Season: season ended, analysis and clearance. Closed: season archived.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Season Master

attributes.name: season_type
attributes.description: Classification of the season by merchandising cycle (e.g., spring/summer, fall/winter, holiday, back-to-school). Drives assortment planning and buying strategies.

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: The date when the season officially begins for merchandising and planning purposes. Marks the start of in-season operations.
attributes.references: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (ORMS) - Season Master

attributes.name: target_gmroi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Target Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI)
attributes.description: The target GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Investment) ratio for the season. Measures the profitability of inventory investment. Key performance metric for merchandising effectiveness.

attributes.name: target_inventory_turns
attributes.description: The target number of times inventory should turn over during the season. Higher turns indicate more efficient inventory management. Key metric for supply chain and merchandising performance.

attributes.name: target_sell_through_rate
attributes.description: The target percentage of seasonal inventory that should be sold at full price before markdowns begin. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 75.00 for 75%). Drives inventory planning and markdown timing.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when the season record was last modified. Audit trail for change tracking and data governance.

products.name: otb_budget
products.description: Open to Buy (OTB) budget record representing the financial control mechanism that governs merchandise buying spend. Tracks planned receipts at cost, actual receipts, committed orders (on-order), available OTB balance, and budget adjustments (transfers, increases, decreases) by department, category, buyer, and season. Updated in near-real-time as buying orders are placed. The authoritative record for whether a buyer has remaining budget authority to commit new purchases. Sourced from ORMS and reconciled with SAP S/4HANA MM.

attributes.name: otb_budget_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the Open to Buy budget record. Primary key for the OTB budget entity.

attributes.name: assortment_plan_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchandise assortment plan that this OTB budget supports. Links budget allocation to the strategic assortment depth and breadth decisions.

attributes.name: budget_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.finance_budget. Business justification: OTB budgets must reconcile to finance-approved budgets — a core retail financial control. Finance teams approve OTB spend limits that must align with finance_budget revenue and COGS projections. This

attributes.name: buyer_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchandise buyer responsible for managing this OTB budget. The buyer has authority to commit purchases within the available budget balance.

attributes.name: category_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchandise category within the department for which this OTB budget applies. Categories provide finer product segmentation (e.g., Men's Shirts, Laptops, Bedding).

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: OTB budgets represent financial commitments that must be tracked against cost centers for expense management and budget control. Retail finance requires cost center assignment on OTB budgets for depar

attributes.name: financial_period_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.financial_period. Business justification: OTB budgets are period-specific financial commitments (fiscal_period, fiscal_year stored as plain attrs). A proper FK to financial_period enables period-close OTB reconciliation, AP accrual matching,

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: OTB budgets map to specific GL accounts (inventory, COGS) for financial posting when purchase orders are received. Required for three-way match, GL coding, and financial statement preparation.

attributes.name: item_hierarchy_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.item_hierarchy. Business justification: OTB budgets are allocated to specific merchandise hierarchy nodes. Essential for buyer authority limits, budget reconciliation, receipt planning, and financial control in retail buying operations and

attributes.name: merch_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to merchandising.merch_plan. Business justification: OTB budgets are financial control mechanisms created within the scope of a merchandise financial plan. The merch_plan sets the overall OTB budget amount and financial targets; individual otb_budget re

attributes.name: profit_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.profit_center. Business justification: OTB budgets must be assigned to profit centers for P&L reporting by business unit. Retail finance teams track OTB spend and receipt commitments by profit center to manage gross margin by channel or di

attributes.name: season_id
attributes.description: Reference to the merchandise season or planning period for which this OTB budget is allocated (e.g., Spring 2024, Holiday 2024, Back-to-School 2024).

attributes.name: actual_receipts_at_cost
attributes.description: The total actual merchandise receipts at cost that have been received into inventory during this budget period. Updated as goods receipts are posted from purchase orders.

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: The approval status of the OTB budget. Pending = awaiting review; Approved = authorized for buyer use; Rejected = not approved and requires revision.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the merchandising leader or financial controller who approved this OTB budget. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this OTB budget was approved. Marks the point at which the budget became active and available for buyer commitments.

attributes.name: available_otb_balance
attributes.description: The remaining budget balance available for new purchase commitments. Calculated as: Planned Receipts + Adjustments - Actual Receipts - Committed Amount. This is the authoritative field that determines whether a buyer can place new orders.

attributes.name: budget_adjustment_amount
attributes.description: The cumulative net adjustment to the original planned receipts budget. Includes increases, decreases, and transfers from other budgets. Positive values increase available OTB; negative values decrease it.

attributes.name: budget_decrease_amount
attributes.description: The total amount of budget decreases applied to this OTB budget. Decreases may occur due to lower-than-expected sales, inventory overstock, or strategic reallocation to other categories.

attributes.name: budget_end_date
attributes.description: The effective end date of the OTB budget period. After this date, the budget is typically closed and no further commitments are allowed unless extended.

attributes.name: budget_increase_amount
attributes.description: The total amount of budget increases applied to this OTB budget. Increases are typically approved by senior merchandising leadership to support higher-than-planned demand or strategic opportunities.

attributes.name: budget_start_date
attributes.description: The effective start date of the OTB budget period. Buyers can begin committing purchases on or after this date.

attributes.name: budget_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the OTB budget. Draft = under planning; Active = buyers can commit purchases; Frozen = temporarily locked for review; Closed = planning period ended; Cancelled = budget withdrawn.

attributes.name: budget_transfer_in_amount
attributes.description: The total amount of budget transferred into this OTB budget from other budgets. Transfers allow buyers to reallocate funds between categories or departments within the same season.

attributes.name: budget_transfer_out_amount
attributes.description: The total amount of budget transferred out of this OTB budget to other budgets. Recorded as a positive value; reduces the available OTB balance of this budget.

attributes.name: committed_amount
attributes.description: The total amount committed on open purchase orders that have not yet been received. Also known as on-order amount. Represents future obligations against the OTB budget.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this OTB budget record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which all monetary amounts in this OTB budget are expressed (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP, CAD).

attributes.name: fiscal_period
attributes.description: The fiscal period (month or quarter) within the fiscal year for which this OTB budget is allocated. Typically 1-12 for monthly periods or 1-4 for quarterly periods.

attributes.name: fiscal_year
attributes.description: The fiscal year to which this OTB budget applies (e.g., 2024). Used for multi-year budget tracking and financial planning alignment.

attributes.name: gmroi_target
attributes.business_glossary_term: Gross Margin Return on Investment (GMROI) Target
attributes.description: The target GMROI ratio for this OTB budget. GMROI measures the gross margin dollars returned for every dollar invested in inventory. Used to evaluate buying efficiency and profitability.

attributes.name: inventory_turn_target
attributes.description: The target inventory turnover rate for merchandise purchased under this OTB budget. Represents the number of times inventory is sold and replaced during the budget period.

attributes.name: last_reconciliation_date
attributes.description: The date when this OTB budget was last reconciled with SAP S/4HANA MM purchase order and goods receipt data. Used to ensure data consistency between ORMS and ERP systems.

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this OTB budget record was last modified. Updated in near-real-time as purchase orders are placed, goods are received, or budget adjustments are made.

attributes.name: markdown_budget_pct
attributes.description: The planned markdown percentage allocated for this OTB budget. Represents the expected price reductions as a percentage of planned receipts at retail. Used for margin planning and promotional strategy.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments about this OTB budget. May include rationale for adjustments, special instructions, or strategic context for the buyer.

attributes.name: planned_receipts_at_cost
attributes.description: The total planned merchandise receipts at cost for this budget period. Represents the initial budget allocation before any adjustments or commitments. Expressed in the budget currency.

attributes.name: sell_through_target_pct
attributes.description: The target sell-through rate (as a percentage) for merchandise purchased under this OTB budget. Represents the percentage of inventory expected to be sold during the budget period.

products.name: buying_order
products.description: Merchandise buying order representing a committed purchase from a supplier for specific SKUs, quantities, and delivery windows. Captures order type (initial buy, reorder, opportunistic), planned receipt date, FOB terms, cost per unit, total order value, and approval status. Distinct from operational purchase orders — this is the buying decision record in ORMS.

attributes.name: buying_order_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the merchandise buying order record in ORMS (Oracle Retail Merchandising System). Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: assortment_plan_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to merchandising.assortment_plan. Business justification: Buying orders are the execution mechanism for assortment plans — a buyer places buying orders to fulfill the SKU commitments defined in an assortment plan. This relationship enables tracking of assort

attributes.name: buyer_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the merchandise buyer or purchasing agent responsible for creating and managing this buying order. Links to workforce/employee master data.

attributes.name: category_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the product category within the department. Enables category-level assortment analysis and GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Investment) tracking.

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Purchase orders for fixtures, supplies, or capital items are allocated to cost centers for capex vs opex classification and budget tracking. Required for non-inventory purchase cost allocation.

attributes.name: department_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the merchandise department for which this buying order is placed. Used for category management and assortment planning.

attributes.name: destination_location_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the specific distribution center, store, or cross-dock facility where the merchandise will be received. Links to inventory node or store master data.

attributes.name: financial_period_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.financial_period. Business justification: Buying orders are reconciled to financial periods for AP accruals, OTB tracking, and period-close reporting. Retail finance teams require buying orders to reference the financial period of planned rec

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Purchase orders post to specific GL accounts (inventory, prepaid, expense) when goods are received. Essential for three-way match, accrual accounting, and financial statement accuracy.

attributes.name: otb_budget_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the OTB (Open to Buy) budget allocation against which this buying order is committed. Used to track spending against merchandise financial plans and prevent over-buying.

attributes.name: receiving_fulfillment_node_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fulfillment.node. Business justification: Inbound purchase orders must specify receiving DC/warehouse for inventory routing and capacity planning. Retail operations require knowing which fulfillment node will process incoming vendor shipments

attributes.name: season_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to merchandising.season. Business justification: Buying orders are executed within specific retail seasons for merchandise planning and OTB budget tracking. Currently has season_code (STRING) which should be normalized to season_id FK. This links bu

attributes.name: supply_purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supplychain.purchase_order. Business justification: Retail buying orders (merchandising procurement intent) are executed as supply chain purchase orders. Buyers track PO execution status, receipt variance, and landed cost reconciliation. This link enab

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the supplier from whom the merchandise is being purchased. Links to the supplier master data in MDM (Master Data Management).

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the buying order received final approval from authorized buyer or merchandise manager. Nullable for orders still in draft or pending approval status.

attributes.name: approval_workflow_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the approval workflow instance used to authorize this buying order. Tracks multi-level approvals based on order value thresholds and buyer authority limits.

attributes.name: cancel_date
attributes.description: Date when the buying order was cancelled. Nullable for active orders. Populated when order_status transitions to cancelled.

attributes.name: cancellation_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized code indicating the reason for order cancellation. Nullable for active orders. Used for supplier performance analysis and procurement process improvement.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this buying order record was first created in ORMS. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the buying order cost and pricing (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Used for multi-currency procurement and financial reporting.

attributes.name: destination_type
attributes.description: Type of destination location where the merchandise will be delivered: distribution center for centralized receiving, store for direct store delivery (DSD), cross_dock for immediate transfer, or vendor_direct for drop-ship to customer.

attributes.name: duty_cost
attributes.description: Estimated or actual customs duty and import taxes for international shipments. Used to calculate landed cost and COGS (Cost of Goods Sold).

attributes.name: exchange_rate
attributes.description: Exchange rate applied to convert supplier currency to base reporting currency at the time of order creation. Used for financial consolidation and P&L (Profit and Loss) reporting.

attributes.name: fob_terms
attributes.description: Incoterms defining the point at which ownership and risk transfer from supplier to retailer. Determines freight responsibility and cost allocation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fob_origin|fob_destination|exw|fca|cif|dap|ddp — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: freight_cost
attributes.description: Estimated or actual freight and shipping cost for transporting the merchandise from supplier to destination. May be retailer-paid or supplier-paid depending on FOB terms.

attributes.name: landed_cost
attributes.description: Total cost of merchandise including product cost, freight, duties, and other charges to deliver goods to the distribution center. Used for margin analysis and pricing decisions.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this buying order record was last updated in ORMS. Tracks the most recent change to any field in the order.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes and special instructions for the buying order. May include packaging requirements, labeling instructions, quality specifications, or other supplier communications.

attributes.name: order_date
attributes.description: Date when the buying order was created and committed in ORMS. Represents the business event timestamp for the buying decision.

attributes.name: order_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the buying order. Human-readable order number used in communications with suppliers and internal stakeholders.

attributes.name: order_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the buying order in the procurement workflow. Tracks progression from draft through approval, submission to supplier, acknowledgment, receipt, and closure or cancellation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|pending_approval|approved|submitted|acknowledged|in_transit|partially_received|received|closed|cancelled — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: order_type
attributes.description: Classification of the buying order indicating the strategic purpose: initial buy for new assortment, reorder for replenishment, opportunistic for special deals, seasonal for seasonal merchandise, promotional for promotion-driven buys, or clearance for end-of-season purchases.

attributes.name: payment_terms
attributes.description: Negotiated payment terms with the supplier (e.g., Net 30, Net 60, 2/10 Net 30). Defines the payment due date and any early payment discounts.

attributes.name: planned_receipt_date
attributes.description: Target date by which the merchandise is expected to arrive at the distribution center or store. Used for inventory planning and assortment timing.

attributes.name: ship_window_end_date
attributes.description: Latest date the supplier must ship the merchandise to meet planned receipt date. Defines the end of the acceptable shipping window; late shipments may incur chargebacks.

attributes.name: ship_window_start_date
attributes.description: Earliest date the supplier is authorized to ship the merchandise. Defines the beginning of the acceptable shipping window for timely assortment flow.

attributes.name: submission_date
attributes.description: Date when the approved buying order was transmitted to the supplier via EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) or other communication channel.

attributes.name: total_order_cost
attributes.description: Total cost value of the buying order in the base currency, calculated as sum of (unit cost × quantity) across all line items. Represents the committed spend with the supplier, excluding freight and duties.

attributes.name: total_order_quantity
attributes.description: Total quantity of units ordered across all SKUs (Stock Keeping Units) in this buying order. Aggregated from line-level quantities.

attributes.name: vendor_order_number
attributes.description: Supplier's own order reference number assigned when they acknowledge the buying order. Used for order tracking and supplier communication.

products.name: buying_order_line
products.description: Line-level detail of a merchandise buying order capturing individual SKU commitments including SKU/UPC, ordered quantity, unit cost, retail price, planned margin, delivery date, and allocation by store cluster. Enables SKU-level OTB tracking and receipt planning.

attributes.name: buying_order_line_id
